summary.text: A twin prime is a prime that is 2 less or 2 more than another prime, such as either member of the pair (17, 19) or (41, 43).
Whether there are infinitely many twin primes is one of the great open questions in number theory, and it is called the twin prime conjecture.
In 2013 Yitang Zhang proved there are infinitely many prime pairs differing by some number below 70 million, and that bound has since been cut to 246.

facts.label: Between the twins
facts.value: Beyond (3, 5), the number between them is a multiple of 6

facts.label: Pair sums
facts.value: Any pair other than (3, 5) adds to a multiple of 12

items.prompt: A classmate says 7 and 11 are twin primes, since both are prime. What is missing?

options.label: Twin primes must both be even
Twin primes must differ by two, and these differ by four
Twin primes must add up to a prime
Twin primes must be next to a multiple of ten

items.explain: A twin prime has a prime gap of two: it is 2 less or 2 more than another prime.

items.prompt: The prime 5 sits in two twin pairs, (3, 5) and (5, 7). Can any larger prime sit in two twin pairs?

options.label: No, five is the only prime that does
Yes, every twin prime does
Yes, but only primes ending in 3
Only if it is larger than a million

items.explain: Five is the only prime in two pairs, because every twin pair beyond (3, 5) has a multiple of 6 between its two primes.

items.prompt: A friend says mathematicians proved after Zhang's 2013 work that infinitely many twin primes exist. Is that right?

options.label: Yes, Zhang proved it outright
Yes, it was shown by computer search
No, substantial progress has been made but it remains unsolved
No, it was shown that only finitely many exist

items.explain: Zhang, Maynard, Tao and others made substantial progress, but the twin prime conjecture is unsolved.

items.prompt: What exactly did Zhang's 2013 announcement show?

options.label: There are infinitely many pairs of primes differing by two
There are no pairs of primes differing by two beyond a point
Every pair of consecutive primes differs by under 70 million
Some gap below 70 million occurs between infinitely many prime pairs

items.explain: He proved there is some integer N under 70 million for which infinitely many pairs of primes differ by N, without saying N is 2.

items.prompt: Researchers have shown that infinitely many prime pairs lie within some fixed distance. What would turn that into the twin prime conjecture?

options.label: Cutting the allowed distance down to 2
Finding one more twin prime pair
Doubling the allowed distance
Proving that 5 is the only repeated prime

items.explain: The bound stands at 246 at most, and improving it to 2 would prove the twin prime conjecture.

items.prompt: What do you know about the number sitting exactly between two twin primes, other than between 3 and 5?

options.label: It is a multiple of 6
It is an odd number
It is a multiple of 4
It is itself a prime

items.explain: Every twin prime pair beyond (3, 5) has the form (6n − 1, 6n + 1) for some natural number n.
